narrative.overview:
Every workspace is a metro line leaving the base branch. Its colour and its number follow it everywhere (sidebar stub, badge, header branch pill, panel tabs, tool stations in the thread) so the developer never loses track of which agent they are looking at. The ground is a white transit-signage sheet: ink type, grey surfaces, hairline rules; colour is spent only on line identity and on the one signal that needs a human.

Density is that of a tool used for hours: 14px body, 13px controls, a 288px map sidebar, a thread capped at 72ch, a diff/terminal panel on the right. Type is Figtree at heavy weights (700/800) for names and controls, like station signage; JetBrains Mono for code, branches and paths only, with ligatures off. Figures are tabular everywhere. Dark theme mirrors the same roles on a near-black ground (#111315) via `prefers-color-scheme`, lifting the darkest line colours (blue, brown, plum) so they still read.

The world rejects the category default of a dark grey ground with a single violet accent and anonymous status dots.
keyCharacteristics: The sidebar list is the map: grey trunk, hollow terminus for the base branch, coloured stubs to round numbered badges.
Line number = ⌘ shortcut = line colour (8 colours, then they loop).
Ink is the only primary; red is the only alarm.
Flat sheet, hairline borders; shadows only on floating overlays.
One inline-SVG icon set on a 16px grid, 1.75 stroke.

rules.name: The Identity Rule
rules.body: Line colours mean "this workspace" and nothing else. Never use one for a state, a button, a link or decoration.

rules.name: The One Alarm Rule
rules.body: Signal Red means a human is needed now (pending permission) or something failed. Running is ink, new is an ink dot on an outlined pill, failed is a red outline with an x.

rules.name: The Ink Primary Rule
rules.body: Exactly one ink-filled button per action group (PR in the header, Envoyer in the composer, Lancer in the run bar); every other action is ghost.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Machines Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono only for code, diffs, branches, paths and terminals; never for UI labels.

rules.name: The No Ligatures Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-ligatures: none` on every code surface; `!=` and `->` must look like what was typed.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is above the page" (dialog, toast). Rows, cards and panels never get one.

rules.name: The Station Rule
rules.body: Circles are stations: a filled circle is a line badge or a completed tool, a hollow 2px ring is the terminus or a pending tool. Don't use circles as generic bullets or avatars.

dos: Do route every identity colour through the `lnN` class and the `--c` property, so badge, stub, station dot and tabs badge always agree.
Do keep numbering = ⌘ shortcut = colour: line number is the workspace's position in the live list, colour loops every 8.
Do put ink numerals on the light line colours (yellow, orange, mint, pink) and test any new line colour for numeral contrast before shipping it.
Do use the inline-SVG set at 16px / 1.75 stroke for any new icon, drawn on the same grid.
Do disable ligatures on every new code surface.
donts: Don't use a line colour for status, emphasis, links or buttons.
Don't use Signal Red for anything that isn't a pending human decision or a failure (diff deletions keep their own diff-del tokens).
Don't add a second filled primary button to an action group, or a brand accent colour beside ink.
Don't add shadows to rows, cards or panels; depth on the sheet is a hairline.
Don't use emoji, text glyphs or an icon font as icons.
Don't set UI labels in JetBrains Mono.
